foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Energy repricing from Red Sea maritime disruption will remain elevated at 65% probability over 30 days, driven by 58% energy supply shock pressure and 76% state confirmation from 5 urgent critical signals.
foil.perspective_strategic: The 58% pressure and 76% state confirmation indicate a strong but not certain transmission path through energy supply shock, with 5 urgent critical signals reinforcing the risk.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The 75% confidence level still leaves room for reversal, and the Iraq oil production surge to 2019 high suggests alternative supply routes could mitigate Red Sea disruption effects.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 65%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through energy supply shock, with 58% pressure and 76% state confirmation

This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
